purpose: Per-file named causes for corpus files that are NOT passing. Exists to remove the ~35min triage phase that every wave-2 agent paid independently and then threw away. A brief MUST draw its worklist from here rather than asking an agent to re-triage. Entries are what the agent that filed them measured; a stale entry is a bug -- re-derive before budgeting.
provenance: wave-2 agents w2/agent-1 (tls), w2/agent-2 (http), w2/agent-3 (fs), round 10; tls per-file causes extracted from the r10-j6 full run logs at integration (155 non-pass tls/https: 119 fail, 19 timeout, 17 self-skip); http/http2 per-file causes extracted the same way (165 'fail' files)
how_to_use: Group by `cause`, count files per cause, budget mechanisms x 10min + 55min overhead. Do NOT budget by subsystem -- see compat/README.md 'Allocate agents by cause family, not by subsystem'.
caveat: Coverage is uneven: the fs inventory is per-file and complete (58 files); tls and http are recorded at cause-shape granularity because that is the level their agents reported. Filling the tls/http per-file rows is itself a cheap, high-leverage task.

fs-watch.CORRECTION: The mechanism this entry used to name -- 'a watcher registers as a pollable but holds no fd, so the drain's stall clock never advances' -- was a MANIFESTATION, not a cause, and not one shared mechanism. Measured: the three hangs had three unrelated semantic causes. recursive:'1' was not validated, so a persistent watcher that should never have existed pinned the loop. decodeName ignored every encoding but 'buffer', so the hex watcher never recognised its own filename and its done never fired. The recursive-promise async iterator had to REJECT with ABORT_ERR rather than end cleanly. Nothing in the event loop was touched. I recorded the manifestation as a cause because I inherited the phrasing from an agent report without testing it -- the fifth instance of this error class in this project and the first one I put into the inventory myself.

remaining.test-fs-watchfile-bigint: mbun loads node's REAL internal/fs/utils, so deepStrictEqual fails on PROTOTYPE IDENTITY before comparing keys -- NOT the '4 Date properties' this entry previously claimed. Changing only the constructor would desynchronise statSync from new Stats() and risk green test-fs-stat-* files.

tls-protocol-method-validation.cause: SSLv2_method/SSLv3_method and friends must be rejected with ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_METHOD.
tls-protocol-method-validation.CORRECTION: My named cause was stale. SSLv2_method/SSLv3_method -> ERR_TLS_INVALID_PROTOCOL_METHOD ALREADY WORKED; those subcases were passing in the logs. The real blockers were (a) secureProtocol version-window semantics -- node does not pass min=max=0 to SecureContext::Init; common.js always passes toV(minVersion, DEFAULT_MIN) and crypto_context.cc adjusts per method, so SSLv23_method lowers only the CEILING to TLS 1.2 and keeps the default floor -- and (b) --tls-min-v1.x is NOT last-flag-wins: lib/tls.js is a fixed if/else chain, so the WIDEST flag wins wherever it sits. I had briefed last-flag-wins explicitly and that was wrong. Also the cluster is 6-for-1: five of the six are 4-line wrappers that require('./test-tls-min-max-version.js'). Size right, cause wrong.

tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.signature: Uniform across all 12: NET.pending=0, handles=3, items=3 -- one listening Server plus the client/server socket pair, and BOTH sockets readable=true writable=true destroyed=false _paused=false _wq=0. Nothing queued, nothing paused, both ends open and idle.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.cause: A genuinely stalled exchange: each side is waiting for bytes the other will never send. NOT an event-loop bug -- node would hold the loop here identically. This is the fifth independent confirmation that hangs in this project are protocol-semantics gaps rather than handle-lifetime bugs.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.hypothesis_i_checked_and_REFUTED: I read NET.pending=0 as 'no fd is in the poll set, so arriving bytes never wake the loop', which would have made all 12 one bug. js_net.cppm:138 says pending counts bounded in-flight operations (e.g. a fetch awaiting its response), NOT poll-set membership. What holds the loop is _held/_loopOpen, both true here. pending=0 is normal. Do not brief an agent on the poll-set theory.
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.confidence: CLASS named and uniform; NOT a single mechanism
tls-timeout-shape-B-stalled-exchange.action: largest tls block. Budget per file or per small group, not as one sweep -- and note it is dominated by abort/destroy/attach-timing cases, which suggests the shared theme is teardown DURING handshake rather than steady-state transfer

verify-error-code-mapping-CROSS-SUBSYSTE.cause: mbun surfaces OpenSSL verify code 20 (UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY, 'issuer not found locally') where node surfaces 21 (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE, 'chain has one non-self-signed cert'). One file surfaces null instead of any code. The two codes differ by how a one-cert chain is treated, so this is chain-depth / X509_STORE flag handling, not a trust-store contents problem.
verify-error-code-mapping-CROSS-SUBSYSTE.confidence: CAUSE named -- the actual/expected pair identifies it uniquely
verify-error-code-mapping-CROSS-SUBSYSTE.action: BEST cluster currently known: 9 files, one mechanism, and it is a correctness fix (chain verification), not a workaround
verify-error-code-mapping-CROSS-SUBSYSTE.cross_subsystem_note: Found separately in two subsystems and only recognised as one cause when the http logs were parsed the same way as the tls logs. tls shows it as 'UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY vs UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE'; http2 shows it as the plain message 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. Same OpenSSL verify path. This is exactly what cluster_finder.py's cross-subsystem ranking exists to catch, and a per-subsystem brief would have split it and under-budgeted both halves.

status_after_fix.why_the_fuller_fix_was_declined: node gets the right code by letting verification run to completion (VerifyCallback returns 1 unconditionally) and checking SSL_get_verify_result() afterwards. mbun passes nullptr to SSL_CTX_set_verify, so OpenSSL's abort IS the enforcement of rejectUnauthorized. Switching to an always-continue callback moves that gate out of OpenSSL into the JS layer, and proving the JS gate airtight on every path (server-side client-cert auth, SNI contexts, session resumption) is a much larger audit whose failure mode is a SILENT VERIFICATION BYPASS. Anyone taking that on must treat it as a security change with its own review, not as a corpus fix.
status_after_fix.measured: guard 681 files (all tls/https/http2/crypto): 0 green->non-green, +3, 1 fail->timeout characterised above

native-entry-points-gated-only-in-the-js.cause: A --permission check placed in the JS shim rather than at the native boundary. Verified on the pre-fix binary: fs.watch('/etc') was correctly DENIED, but the raw globalThis.__mbunWatchNative.start('/etc') returned a watch descriptor. Every test that went through fs.watch therefore made the runtime look correctly gated.

Any other __mbun*Native global whose check lives only in its JS wrapper has the same hole. AUDIT ACTION: enumerate every __mbun*Native global and probe each raw method under --permission, not through its public wrapper.
native-entry-points-gated-only-in-the-js.action: standing audit item; the fs.watch instance is fixed and independently re-verified

http-timeout-shape-D-DELETED-DID-NOT-EXI.cause: DELETED. This entry claimed 2 http files died in native WTFCrashWithInfo. Measured: all 49 remaining test-http* timeouts exit 124 (the harness timeout kill) and NOT ONE of their logs contains WTFCrash/SIGSEGV/SIGABRT/Segmentation text. The reasoning that settles it: a crashing process exits on a signal, so it never reaches the timeout kill at all -- a crash and a 124 are mutually exclusive classifications.
http-timeout-shape-D-DELETED-DID-NOT-EXI.how_the_error_got_in: A wave-2 agent reported 'no dump / native WTFCrashWithInfo (2)' and I recorded it as a cause without checking. 'hang_dump produced no dump' is not evidence of a crash; for http it turned out one of the two was hang_dump's own limitation (see below). This is the manifestation-as-cause error again, propagated by me from an agent report -- the same way the fs-watch entry went wrong.

http-destroySoon-is-immediate-destroy.cause: Socket.destroySoon() is implemented as an immediate destroy(). Response 1 carries maxRequestsOnConnectionReached -> res._last -> destroySoon(), which closes the fd synchronously inside onHead, so the pipelined request 2 is never dispatched and dropRequest never fires. node's destroySoon is end() followed by destroy on 'finish'.

http-client-connect-ignores-options-sign.cause: options.signal is honoured only by Server.listen (js_net.cppm:849); Socket.prototype.connect has no equivalent, so an aborted signal never produces the AbortError on the socket.
http-client-connect-ignores-options-sign.caveat: The test asserts listenerCount(signal,'abort') === 1 SYNCHRONOUSLY, which node's own nextTick registration appears not to satisfy -- verify against real node before budgeting.

http-server-socket-error-listener-is-a-n.cause: The server connection's 'error' listener is a noop (js_net.cppm:3068) instead of node's socketOnError, so a user's res.socket.emit('error', ...) is swallowed and the response is never torn down. Related: the parser is not re-armed after a clientError the server claimed, so only the first invalid byte errors where one test needs 21.
http-server-socket-error-listener-is-a-n.action: Cheap but WIDE: routing all server-socket errors through socketOnError makes every ECONNRESET emit 'clientError', which is what node does. Guard broadly.

tls-session-and-ticket-support-ABSENT.cause: TLS session resumption is entirely absent, not partially wrong. js_tls_live.cppm:533 `getSession() { return undefined; }`, :562 `setSession() { return this; }`, and js_https_live.cppm:24 states outright that the reactor never emits 'session'. One mechanism covers all of it: SSL_CTX_sess_set_new_cb + session serialisation + the 'session' event + the `session:` connect option.
tls-session-and-ticket-support-ABSENT.provenance: Found by w4/agent-tls, which called it the densest lead it saw. The inventory did NOT have this cluster at all -- its 8 files sat split across three other buckets, so every previous brief under-budgeted all three. A cause that spans buckets is invisible to per-bucket ranking.

ipv6-listen-not-implemented-NET-LAYER.cause: net_parse_addr (modules/jsc/src/runtime/net.inc:45) only ever builds a sockaddr_in and MAPS '::' and '::1' onto IPv4 ANY/loopback, so listen(0, '::1') silently binds IPv4. Blocks test-tls-connect-address-family and test-https-connect-address-family, and almost certainly several test-net-* files.
ipv6-listen-not-implemented-NET-LAYER.action: NOT a TLS bug -- do not budget it to a tls agent. Needs a net-layer round that measures its own reach first.
